what: Hinge Health treats muscle and joint pain remotely. Employees of its client companies do guided exercise programmes at home with sensors and an app, supervised by physical therapists, instead of attending clinics.
customers: Large employers and health plans, which pay per enrolled member to reduce surgery and physiotherapy costs.
money: per-member fees for the digital musculoskeletal programme
moat: Contracts with large employers and the clinical evidence that the programme reduces surgeries, which is what a benefits manager needs before switching a population onto it.
risks: A reported net loss on an operating basis, with stock compensation after the 2025 listing
11 times sales for a company whose contracts renew annually
Employers can cut digital health benefits quickly when budgets tighten
opportunities: $322M of free cash flow, which is unusual for a recently listed health technology company
Revenue grew from $293M to $588M in two years and is $801M over the last twelve months
$364M of cash against $8M of debt, and analysts see about 25% upside
watch: Enrolled member growth and contract renewal rates with large employers.
